articles.summary: Malaysia Airlines said on 31 October that customer data handled by reservation provider Amadeus between August 2023 and September 2026 may be affected, while its own systems were not compromised. Amadeus patched a booking-display flaw; Japanese, Korean and Hong Kong carriers also reported exposure. No payment data is reported accessed.
articles.title: Amadeus fixes booking system vulnerability amid airline data breaches

articles.summary: Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil said on 18 November that no significant threats to citizens' data or digital infrastructure had been found, and that reports of Malaysian data on dark web sites are unverified and may be old. He also said MCMC and Nacsa must move telcos towards quantum-safe networks.
articles.title: No major cyber threats affecting Malaysians detected so far, says Fahmi

articles.summary: On 4 November the National Security Council raised the National Cyber Security Threat Level from Low to Medium as a precaution. Operators of national critical information infrastructure were told to tighten monitoring, report weekly to NACSA even without incidents, and isolate critical operational systems from external networks.
articles.title: Nacsa raises level of cyber security threat to medium

articles.summary: Several Bank Rakyat web pages, including the iRakyat login page, were defaced late on 6 November in a suspected cyberattack claimed by a group calling itself MARLANWG. The communications minister said online banking in general remains safe. The bank had not said whether customer data was affected.
articles.title: Fahmi says online banking remains safe despite cyberattacks and Bank Rakyat hack

articles.summary: The Health Ministry disclosed on 12 November a breach limited to a supporting file storage and sharing platform at one of its facilities. It says patient treatment and health services continue as normal. Investigation continues, and a third-party tracker also lists an unconfirmed claim against the ministry's domain.
articles.title: Health Ministry reports cyber breach at facility, services unaffected

articles.summary: Bank Negara Malaysia governor Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said on 18 November that cyber incidents and even banking outages should be expected as finance becomes more interconnected. The central bank is tightening supervision, updating its Risk Management in Technology policy and working with NACSA, while urging banks to keep investing in detection and recovery.
articles.title: Bank Negara warns cyber attacks and banking disruptions will become more common

articles.summary: FinCEN posted a website alert on 25 November saying it is investigating a cybersecurity incident that has disrupted some of its services. The agency has not said which services are affected or when the incident began, and it is unclear whether it is linked to other recent US government outages.
articles.title: Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network investigating 'cybersecurity incident'

articles.summary: Japanese home-furnishings retailer Nitori said on 9 November that up to 37.62 million customer records may have leaked after unauthorised access confirmed on 6 November. A third-party probe dates the intrusion to mid-to-late October. Emails and addresses were exposed; passwords and card data were not. Customers were warned of phishing.
articles.title: Cyberattack puts 37.62 million Nitori customer records at risk

articles.summary: A district hospital in Thuringia lost systems on the evening of 14 November and its emergency room went offline the next morning after an extortion message arrived. Emergency patients were redirected, and the ER began reopening on 16 November. Police are investigating; whether patient data was taken is unknown.
articles.title: Germany: Greiz Hospital Reopens Emergency Room After Ransom Attack

articles.summary: Equinor, Norway's state-controlled energy company, confirmed on 17 November an ongoing cyberattack against internal IT systems. The company said production continues without interruption. Details of the intrusion, its source and any data loss had not been disclosed in coverage available at publication.
articles.title: Norwegian Gas Giant Equinor Says It's Under Cyberattack. Production Keeps Running

articles.summary: Portugal's energy agency ADENE took its building energy certification system and online portal offline as a precaution after a cyberattack, reported on 24 November. Certificates issued before the incident remain valid, but no date has been set for restoring the service. The agency has not published details on the attackers or any data exposure.
articles.title: Cyberattack disrupts energy certification services in Portugal

articles.summary: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard disclosed on 20 November that third-party service providers were targeted in a cyberattack that exposed customer marketing data. Visa said its own systems were not involved and no card payment data was affected. The incident illustrates third-party access risk that is equally relevant to Malaysian banks and card processors.
articles.title: JPMorgan, Visa, Mastercard Say Third-Party Vendors Targeted in Cyberattack

milestones.label: Dewan Rakyat session scheduled to end

articles.summary: Government business at the Dewan Rakyat is scheduled to run from 30 November to 8 December, after Budget committee debates. The order paper lists the Constitution (Amendment) (No. 2) Bill separating the attorney-general and public prosecutor roles, plus bills on courts, prisons, adoption, urban renewal and the Federal Territories mufti. The list may change.
articles.title: Seven bills lined up for Dewan Rakyat from Nov 30

articles.summary: Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong tabled the Finance Bill 2026 and the Tax Collection, Administration and Enforcement Measures Bill 2026 for first reading on 16 November. Both are slated for second reading during the current Dewan Rakyat sitting, which is due to end on 8 December.
articles.title: Two finance bills tabled for first reading

articles.summary: On 30 October the Cabinet approved a two-stage overhaul of the Universities and University Colleges Act. Stage one removes provisions restricting student expression and association, to be tabled in December; stage two drafts an entirely new law, targeted for 2027 without a fixed timeline.
articles.title: Cabinet approves two-stage reform of AUKU, amendments to be tabled in Dec

articles.summary: The Election Commission set the 13th Sarawak state election for 12 December, with nominations on 28 November and early voting on 8 December. 82 seats are contested; the ruling GPS bloc won 76 in 2021. The campaign runs about 14 days and ends 11 December.
articles.title: Sarawak state election set for Dec 12 as 82 seats go up for grabs

articles.summary: The Dewan Rakyat approved Budget 2027 allocations for several more ministries in its seventh sitting week, including Works, Transport, Health and Energy Transition. Eight further ministries are due to wind up next week. Committee-stage debate runs to 26 November, and the meeting is scheduled to end on 8 December.
articles.title: Budget 2027 debate: Eight ministries cleared, eight more to wind up next week

milestones.label: Federal Court hears IRB leave bid in Najib bankruptcy case

articles.summary: The Federal Court fixed 23 February 2027 to hear the Inland Revenue Board's leave application against the Court of Appeal decision that stayed bankruptcy proceedings over roughly RM1.69 billion in tax claims against Najib Razak. The stay was granted in September pending his separate tax appeal.
articles.title: IRB's RM1.69b appeal in Najib bankruptcy case set for Feb 23

articles.summary: The prosecution told the court on 3 November it will call 25 witnesses in the corruption trial of former human resources minister M. Saravanan, who is accused of taking RM1.097 million linked to foreign worker quotas. A conviction carries up to 20 years in prison and a heavy fine.
articles.title: Prosecution to call 25 witnesses in Saravanan's RM1.097m corruption trial

articles.summary: A former employee of a government-linked company was remanded on 12 November over alleged bribes of about RM3 million, in a case being investigated by the MACC Selangor office under Section 16(a)(B) of the MACC Act 2009. No charge had been reported in the sources found.
articles.title: Former GLC Employee Remanded Over Alleged RM3 Mln Bribes

articles.summary: CISA added five Mitel MiCollab flaws to its KEV catalog on 25 November. Accenture's Apex Labs saw them exploited as zero-days in a data-theft campaign: attackers ran commands within minutes, gained root in about 30 minutes and reached backup and database servers within roughly 20 hours. Mitel patched on 16 November.

articles.summary: Vates disclosed on 10 November that a crafted authentication cookie bypasses Xen Orchestra login and returns an admin token, enabling code execution on managed pools and root on XCP-ng hosts. Vates said it was being exploited, with a RedLine-linked server named. CISA added it to KEV on 25 November. A companion import flaw was unfixed.
